description: Catalog of every boolean opt-in/opt-out feature flag across the marketplace. Read by lib/fleet-features.sh (value resolution) and enforced by lib/tests/test-fleet-features.sh (drift gate: every boolean `${NAME:-false|0|off|true|on}` / os.environ.get boolean in plugin source must be catalogued here or in the test's ignore list, and every `default` must match the code). Field reference: fleet-controller/CLAUDE.md, section 'Feature catalog'.

flags.name: FLEETD_SPAWN_ENABLED
flags.summary: fleetd actually spawns ticket workers; without it fleetd only detects and serves its health API.

requires.step: fleet-env-check passes (the worker spawn command CLAUDE_CMD or CLAUDE_BIN resolves); run /fleet-controller:fleet-env-check

flags.why: This is the switch that makes fleetd do work. Without it, dispatch and restarts only queue entries that nothing consumes.

flags.name: FLEET_AUTO_RESTART
flags.summary: Detection escalates a stalled or crashed pipeline all the way to KILL+RESTART instead of stopping at KILL.
flags.why: Unset, the detector and dashboard cap severity at KILL, so a stalled run is killed and left dead. Crash/orphan reconciliation (fleet_can_restart) already restarts by default, which is why the docs call this default-on; the detection escalation path does not. Setting it true makes both paths agree. Restarts stay capped at FLEET_MAX_RESTARTS.

default_exceptions.why: fleet_can_restart (used by orphan reconciliation and fleet_restart_pipeline) treats unset as enabled

flags.name: FLEET_AUTO_DISPATCH
flags.summary: fleetd sweeps for planner epics stamped dispatch=true and enqueues their ready children automatically.
flags.why: Turn on once you trust planner output to start work unattended. Off, every epic waits for an explicit /fleet-controller dispatch or POST /dispatch. The approval gate still stops complex tickets either way.

flags.name: FLEET_AUTO_RESUME_STALLED
flags.summary: Approved children of a dispatched epic that have no live worker and no queue entry get a resume entry enqueued automatically.
flags.why: Closes the gap where a ticket fixed or re-approved outside the pipeline sits idle forever and blocks its blocked_by chain. Off, the finding is only reported. Pairs naturally with FLEET_AUTO_DISPATCH.

flags.name: FLEET_EPIC_AUTO_PR
flags.summary: When every child of a shared-branch epic is Done, fleet-controller opens the epic integration PR per repo (never merges it).

requires.step: gh CLI installed and authenticated on the fleetd host

flags.why: Only matters if your planner emits Branch Directives (shared epic branches). Then it removes a manual step; the PR still needs a human merge.

flags.name: FLEET_BOARD_PUSHER_ENABLE
flags.summary: fleetd periodically drains every ticket's event outbox to the board driver, so the Linear column/labels catch up even when no flow.sh exit drained it.

requires.step: FIRST run ticket-auto-pipeline/skills/ticket-flow/board-cursor-fastforward.sh (dry-run, then real) or the board replays every ticket's full history

flags.why: The board is otherwise only projected at flow.sh exits, so a dead-lettered or missed drain never heals. Safe once cursors are fast-forwarded; dangerous before.

flags.name: FLEET_POSTMORTEM_ON_KILL
flags.summary: Runs the pipeline post-mortem analysis on pipelines the fleet killed, not only on pipelines that finished on their own.
flags.why: Gives killed runs the same failure-signature analysis as finished ones. Off by default because a mass kill would run many analyses at once (network, gh rate limits).

flags.name: FLEET_OTEL_ENABLE
flags.summary: fleetd runs an OpenTelemetry exporter that turns pipeline and agent-activity logs into GenAI spans sent to an OTLP collector.

requires.step: FLEET_OTEL_ENDPOINT points at a reachable OTLP collector (default http://localhost:4318)
pip install -r fleet-controller/fleetd/requirements-otel.txt on the fleetd host

flags.why: Worth it if you run a collector (Langfuse, Jaeger, ...). Strictly downstream: an unreachable collector costs traces and nothing else.

flags.name: FLEET_TRACE_PROPAGATE_ENABLE
flags.summary: Exports a derived TRACEPARENT into each worker so the agent runtime's own spans nest under fleetd's phase span.
flags.why: A refinement on top of OTel export: nicer trace trees, nothing more. Only useful once FLEET_OTEL_ENABLE is on and traces are being read.

flags.name: FLEET_SCORE_EXPORT_ENABLE
flags.summary: fleetd's periodic sweeper posts per-run and per-ticket outcome scores from runs.jsonl to Langfuse.
flags.why: Turn on if you use Langfuse to compare runs. Any missing credential makes it a silent no-op, so check the requirements column.

flags.name: FLEET_OBSERVER_ENABLE
flags.summary: Phase-level workers stream stream-json output and a supervised observer sidecar turns it into deterministic findings.

requires.note: the observer only sees phase-level workers, never ticket-level ones

flags.why: Non-authoritative diagnostics (long tool calls, odd agent behaviour). Has no effect unless phase-level dispatch is on.

flags.name: FLEET_PHASE_DISPATCH_ENABLE
flags.summary: fleetd spawns each phase as its own short-lived worker and sequences phases itself, instead of one long-lived /ticket-auto worker per ticket.
flags.why: Fully implemented but its rollout is not switched on: trial it on one fleetd instance and compare outcomes before relying on it.

flags.name: FLEET_STORE_ENABLE
flags.summary: fleetd keeps its SQLite state store (workers, queue, holds) and detectors read it instead of re-parsing logs.
flags.why: Leave on. false is the pre-store fallback: detectors re-read log files and holds lose their durable row.

flags.name: FLEET_FENCE_ENFORCE
flags.summary: flow.sh refuses transitions from a superseded worker generation, so a zombie worker cannot corrupt ticket state.
flags.why: Leave on. Turning it off is a rollback switch only.

flags.name: FLEET_KILL_VERIFY
flags.summary: Kills escalate through SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL with a liveness re-check after each rung, instead of only writing a stop file.
flags.why: Leave on. false is the legacy stop-file-only kill, which can leave a worker running.

flags.name: FLEET_EPIC_BRANCH_SYNC
flags.summary: Each dispatch cycle merges base-branch changes into shared epic branches so they do not rot.
flags.why: Leave on if you use shared epic branches; it is a no-op otherwise.

flags.name: FLEET_STARTUP_ENV_CHECK
flags.summary: fleetd refuses to start when fleet-env-check.sh reports a problem (bad CLAUDE_CMD, missing LINEAR_API_KEY, ...).
flags.why: Leave on. false exists for fleetd's own subprocess tests.

flags.name: FLEET_WORKER_ISOLATE_SETTINGS
flags.summary: Workers start with project/local settings only, so user-scope plugins (claude-mem, output styles, caveman) cannot seed them with misleading context.
flags.why: Leave on. This fixed workers stopping to ask a nonexistent human after reading stale memory context.

flags.name: FLEET_DRY_RUN
flags.summary: Interventions, dispatches and epic-branch pushes are logged but not executed.
flags.why: For watching a new install's decisions before going live. Leaving it on means the fleet never acts.

flags.name: FLEET_ENV_CHECK_LIVE_PROBE
flags.summary: fleet-env-check spawns one real worker turn to prove permission_denials is empty.
flags.why: A one-off diagnostic when workers are being denied tools; it costs a real worker turn every time the check runs.

flags.name: POSTMORTEM_ENABLED
flags.summary: Every pipeline finalize runs the post-mortem failure-signature analysis.
flags.why: Leave on; it feeds retro and issue filing and is fail-soft.

flags.name: POSTMORTEM_FILE_ISSUES
flags.summary: Post-mortem files a GitHub issue for each new recurring failure signature (rate-limited by POSTMORTEM_ISSUES_PER_HOUR).

requires.step: gh CLI authenticated with write access to GITHUB_ISSUE_REPO (default: the plugin repo itself, which is public)

flags.why: Useful if you maintain the plugins and want failures to arrive as issues. The default target repo is public, so only enable where that is acceptable.

flags.name: EPIC_BRANCH_PUSH_VERIFY
flags.summary: The repo's pre-push hook runs on the epic-branch creation push.
flags.why: That push is identical to origin/<base>, so the hook has nothing to check and would run against whatever the shared clone has checked out.

flags.name: SPAWN_DIAGNOSTICS
flags.summary: spawn-helper.sh installs an ERR trap that logs a META|spawn-crash line with the failing function and line.
flags.why: Turn on only while chasing a spawn-helper crash.

flags.name: VERIFY_SERVED_WORKTREE_ENFORCE
flags.summary: ticket-verify gate-stops when the app on LOCAL_URL is serving a different checkout of a repo under test.
flags.why: Leave on; false downgrades a provably wrong verify (testing someone else's code) to a warning.

flags.name: VERIFY_SERVED_WORKTREE_STRICT
flags.summary: ticket-verify also gate-stops when it cannot tell which checkout is being served (no visible listener, container port).
flags.why: Right for hosts where every served port is a local process. On container-served stacks it would hold every verify.

flags.name: TICKET_CREATE_GUARD
flags.summary: A PreToolUse hook denies direct Linear issue creation and points agents at /ticket-create.
flags.why: Leave on. off is the opt-out for a session that must create issues another way.

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_VPLAN
flags.summary: Missing, short or unverifiable Verification Plan tables (VPLAN_*) make a ticket not-ready instead of advisory.
flags.why: More hand-written tickets get held until someone adds a plan. Planner Refinement already runs strict regardless of this flag, so this only affects tickets checked outside the planner.

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_VERIFICATION
flags.summary: A ticket with no Verification Plan and no AC carrying a concrete expected result is not-ready.
flags.why: A weaker floor than DOR_STRICT_VPLAN: holds only tickets with nothing self-verifying at all.

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_AC_IMPL
flags.summary: A ticket whose every acceptance criterion describes implementation work, with no observable outcome, is not-ready.
flags.why: Catches 'refactor X' style ACs that cannot be verified; holds those tickets until rewritten.

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_CATALOG
flags.summary: A named test user or role that does not resolve against the test-user catalog makes the ticket not-ready.
flags.why: Only useful once your test-user catalog is complete; otherwise it holds tickets for catalog gaps.

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_TEST_DATA
flags.summary: Missing or unsourced test data is a hard not-ready code on legacy-format ticket bodies.
flags.why: Bodies carrying the Source contract are already hard by default; this extends it to older free-form bodies, holding more of them.

default_exceptions.why: on a body carrying the Source contract an unset flag counts as true (TEST_DATA_MISSING hard by default)

flags.name: DOR_STRICT_TEST_DATA_SOURCE
flags.summary: On Source-contract bodies, a test-data item that does not say where it comes from is a hard not-ready code.
flags.why: The one DoR switch that defaults on. false lets you observe unsourced items as advisory while migrating.

flags.name: DOR_SEMANTIC_DRIFT_DEMOTE
flags.summary: Semantic DoR drift findings are demoted to advisory.
flags.why: The planner always passes true on its own call; the library default stays false for every other caller. Nothing to set on a host.

flags.name: PLANNER_REFINEMENT_AUDIT_DEMOTE
flags.summary: In Refinement, a semantic audit dispute that quotes the ticket's own section demotes an allow-listed heuristic DoR code to advisory.
flags.why: Fewer false-positive holds from heuristic codes, at the cost of trusting the audit agent's quote. Try it if planner tickets keep getting held for codes a human would wave through.

flags.name: PLANNER_REQUIRE_INTENT
flags.summary: ticket-planner refuses raw idea strings and only accepts a sealed /grill-me intent file.
flags.why: Turn on if every plan should start from a grilled, sealed intent. Set it in interactive settings, where planning runs.

flags.name: PLANNER_REVIEW_HOLD
flags.summary: Every planner run stops after the Review phase.
flags.why: Legacy spelling of --until Review; pass that flag per run instead of making every run stop.

flags.name: PLANNER_REFINEMENT_SEMANTIC
flags.summary: Refinement runs the two semantic DoR agent passes per ticket on top of the deterministic check.
flags.why: Leave on; false gates on the deterministic verdict alone and saves two agent spawns per ticket.

flags.name: PLANNER_REFINEMENT_DRIFT_CHECK
flags.summary: Refinement compares each child's Linear description against its TicketGen baseline and flags edits.
flags.why: Leave on; false skips one Linear read per child and stops noticing hand edits.
